svg.title: Circular economy effects on European industrial GHG emissions

cc:Work.dc:title: Circular economy effects on European industrial GHG emissions
cc:Work.dc:description: EU-only CE effects on reported European industrial GHG emissions in 2050, with NDC on the left and NDC+LTT on the right. Panels a,b compare source-defined all-industry percentage changes for OMNIA-ENGAGE (left solid bar) and GCAM (right hatched bar), calculated as 100 × (CE industry GHG − no-CE industry GHG) / no-CE industry GHG in the same model, pathway and year. OMNIA selects the reported all-industry parent Emissions|GHG|Industry, including sectors beyond cement, iron and steel, and aluminium; it is not the sum of those three sectors. GCAM sums Emissions|Kyoto Gases|Energy|Demand|Industry and Emissions|Kyoto Gases|Industrial Processes. The inventories' gas coverage, GWP conventions and process boundaries are not documented as harmonised. Scales match between climate columns. Reported negative GHG is retained, and carbon capture is not subtracted again. GCAM has no matching sector GHG/Kyoto aggregates, so no sector breakdown is plotted. Its partial sector CO2 variables cannot reconstruct complete cement, steel and aluminium GHG inventories and are not substituted. Industry decompositions and the separate OMNIA three-sector calculations remain unplotted CSV context, with Plotted=False. Missing sector inputs in that context do not replace the independently reported industry parent. Original source quantities, reference totals, units, variables, regions, missing treatments and coefficients accompany the CSVs. Only medium/high EU-only CE is selected. Geographic boundaries retain the documented OMNIA EU-region versus GCAM EU-27 approximation. No CE is zero by construction, which does not establish agreement in absolute emissions or harmonise source inventories.
